title: Authentication: the Deploy App identity layer
breadcrumb: Authentication: the Deploy App identity layer

headings.text: What Deploy App is (for an integrator)

blocks.html:
TAK Server trusts certificates and groups. On a Deploy App deployment you don't manage either by hand — Deploy App is the identity layer that issues your certificate and governs your groups, and TAK Server is wired to trust it.

What Deploy App is (for an integrator)

Deploy App brings several products (chat, situational awareness/TAK, video, logging…) together behind one identity and one secure web UI. Its shape is:

one identity provider (Keycloak) · one hub API (RASENMAEHER / "rmapi") · a web UI · several products · a certificate/trust layer that lets them talk securely.

The defining rule: a user enrolls once, authenticates with an mTLS client certificate, and reaches every product they are entitled to. The hub fans user-lifecycle events out to each product over mTLS — so revoking a user in one place revokes them everywhere. TAK Server is one of those products.

The pieces

Piece Role
RASENMAEHER (rmapi) The hub API (pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api). Owns the authoritative user and certificate state: enrollment, invite/approval, CSR signing, revocation, token issuance.
Keycloak The OIDC identity provider, and the place where groups are managed (which then flow to TAK Server).
Certificate / trust layer The CA that signs your client cert. Differs per stack: Legacy (Docker Compose) uses CFSSL behind an nginx ingress; Kubernetes (opendefence-platform, alpha) uses cert-manager + trust-manager + opendefense-pki behind Traefik.
Products TAK Server, Matrix, etc. Each trusts the Deploy App CA and the groups Keycloak asserts.

How you authenticate

The Deploy App Core API (rmapi) recognises these credentials (from its OpenAPI securitySchemes):

  • mTLS client certificate — the primary credential. The ingress/proxy terminates mTLS and forwards the verified identity as a header to the services (MTLSHeader / MTLSorJWT / ValidUser schemes). The same certificate authenticates you to TAK Server and to Keycloak.
  • JWT bearer (JWTBearer) — a token for API calls where a cert isn't convenient (e.g. UI-driven flows). Obtained via the token endpoints (see Enrolling & getting a client certificate).

So the integration story is: get a Deploy App client certificate once, then present it to TAK Server's Marti API and CoT stream like any other TAK client — and let Keycloak groups decide what you can see and send.

The Deploy App Core API is documented on this site's own API reference (codename RASENMAEHER); its OpenAPI lives at public/api-specs/rasenmaeher/ in this repo and is served in the embedded reference.
